P-H1.clause: Art. 3 Noon Work Ban: "All work performed directly under the sun and in open places shall not be allowed between the peak hours of 12.30 pm and 3 pm from June 15 to September 15 every year. No business shall be resumed before 3pm"

P-H1a.clause: Art. 11 Prohibition of Work During the Midday: "For technical reasons, the following works are exempt and must continue uninterrupted"; "When technical reasons dictate the continuation of work, employers must provide workers with the following". The attested exempt_reason is a product rule (ADR 0011 P-H1a): an exemption is never inferred

P-H2.daily.clause: Art. 17(1): "The maximum normal working hours for workers shall be (8) eight hours per day or (48) forty-eight hours per week."; Art. 19(1): "do not exceed two hours per day" and "the total working hours shall not exceed (144) one hundred and forty four hours every (3) three weeks."

P-H2.weekly.clause: Art. 17(1): "The maximum normal working hours for workers shall be (8) eight hours per day or (48) forty-eight hours per week."; Art. 19(1): "the total working hours shall not exceed (144) one hundred and forty four hours every (3) three weeks."

P-H3.clause: Art. 18: "The worker may not work for more than (5) five consecutive hours without a break or breaks of not less than an hour in total, provided that these periods are not included in the working hours." PROTECTIVE READING (ADR 0011 P-H3): ban time and ADOSH cycle rest are not credited as the break

P-H4.clause: Art. 21: "The worker shall be granted a paid weekend of not less than one day, according to the employment contract or the work regulation." The one rest day in seven is the reading in ADR 0011 P-H4

P-H5.hours.clause: Art. 5(2)(c): "The actual working hours shall not exceed six hours per day and shall include one break or more, which shall not be less than one hour in total"; Art. 5(2)(f): "The juvenile shall not work overtime"

P-H5.run.clause: Art. 5(2)(c): "this period(s) shall be defined, so that the juvenile does not work for more than four consecutive hours."

P-H5.window.clause: Art. 5(2)(d): "The juvenile shall not work between 7 pm and 7 am."

P-H7.cap60.clause: Table 1: Medium Risk, heavy work "Continuous paced work 45 work - 15 rest"; High Risk "Strict Work/Rest cycling required", light work 45 work - 15 rest, heavy work 20 work - 40 rest. Moderate work uses the heavy column (PROTECTIVE READING, ADR 0046)

P-H7.run.clause: Table 1: Medium Risk, heavy work "Continuous paced work 45 work - 15 rest"; High Risk, light work 45 work - 15 rest, heavy work 20 work - 40 rest

P-H7.lone.clause: Table 1: Medium Risk "Working alone to be avoided"; High Risk "No person to work alone"

P-H7.unacclimatised.clause: Table 1: Medium Risk and High Risk "No unacclimatised person to work"; "Unacclimatised workers are defined as new workers or those who have been off work for more than 14 days due to illness or vacation leave (in a cool climate area)"

P-H8.ramp.clause: Section 3 acclimatisation table: new employee 20% / 40% / 60% / 80% / 100% on days 1-5; experienced employee 50 / 60 / 80 / 100 / 100; re-acclimatisation by days away. The "R/E*" row (4-5 days) is read as 80 then 100 (PROTECTIVE READING, ADR 0011 P-H8)

P-H8.heavy7.clause: CoP 11.0 3.2(b)(i): "with an allowance of 5-7 days for acclimatization before starting hard work in a hot environment"; 7 days is the protective end (ADR 0011 P-H8)

P-H10.clause: P-H10 No added minutes: a plan never schedules more work minutes per worker than the published shift and never extends it. Product rule, not law (ADR 0011 section 4)

STOP.red.clause: Decisions 2 and 8: below the Red edge (red_twl_w_m2) every crew is stopped. POLICY, beyond the ADOSH table: stop work

STOP.no_acclimatised.clause: Table 1: Medium Risk and High Risk "No unacclimatised person to work"; a Medium or High tick is unworkable for a crew with no acclimatized member (ADR 0011 section 2 steps 4 and 6)

FALLBACK.high.clause: Decision 4: with no usable forecast for an hour the hour is fallback and the planner treats every on-shift tick as High, never less protective than the ban (ADR 0011 P-H12)
